observation.visible_scene: First-person POV from a rider on a mat/float (trident-and-arrow patterned mat with a yellow handle at the bottom edge) going through an enclosed, transparent water-slide tube filled with teal water. The rider's legs in black shorts and a dark water shoe are visible at the bottom. Through the clear tube wall on the right is an aquarium-like space with swimming fish (notably yellow-tailed fish and a darker elongated silhouette) and a glowing green rectangular frame plus dark framework. A 'Attractions 360°' watermark sits at the bottom right. In the early frames a forward tunnel with another distant rider is visible ahead.
visible_changes: The camera view pans/rotates rightward over the clip: the forward tunnel and the distant rider move from center to the left edge and exit the frame by about frame 13.
The transparent side wall showing the aquarium takes up progressively more of the frame as the pan continues.
The rider's legs shift from center-bottom toward the left-bottom and partly out of view; the white splashing water around the feet diminishes accordingly.
Fish inside the aquarium move independently of the camera (the yellow-tailed fish and other silhouettes change position and apparent size frame to frame).
The glowing green rectangular frame and the dark structural framework seen through the wall translate leftward across the image as the camera pans.

From roughly frame 28 onward a large, out-of-focus brownish vertical form grows to fill the center-right of the view, and from about frame 33 a curved cream-colored tube seam/edge enters from the left.
Water droplets and streaks on the inner tube surface remain throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The start and end of the slide ride and what occurs before frame 1 or after frame 41.
The identity and motion of the distant rider seen only in the early frames.
uncertain_details: Whether the growing brownish vertical shape is a reflection of the rider/body on the wet tube wall, a support column, or a large fish behind the glass.
Whether the rightward view change is caused by the rider/camera turning or by the curvature of the tube.
Exact species/identities of the fish and the dark elongated silhouette.
